In philosophy , economics , and political science , the common good (also commonwealth , common weal , general welfare , or public benefit ) is either what is shared and beneficial for all or most members of a given community , or alternatively, what is achieved by citizenship, collective action, and active participation in the realm of politics and public service. The concept of the common good differs significantly among philosophical doctrines . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Early conceptions of the common good were set out by Ancient Greek philosophers, including Aristotle and Plato . One understanding of the common good rooted in Aristotle's philosophy remains in common usage today, referring to what one contemporary scholar calls the "good proper to, and attainable only by, the community, yet individually shared by its members." [ 3 ]
